newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Placer served land claim on mine.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Placer served land claim on mine.

text.p: Placer Pacific, 70 percent owned by Placer Dome Inc, said on Wednesday it had been served a native title land claim on its Osborne gold and copper mine in northwest Queensland from the Yullana aboriginal clan.
Placer Pacific corporate communications manager Ian Williams said the company had received the claim about a month ago, but it had not affected production at the mine.
"It hasn't affected anything, it's only just been lodged and it may take years before the outcome is known," Williams told Reuters. He said the mine is based on leased pastoral land.
Under Australia's current native title laws, pastoral leases can extinguish native title claims if it is proven that the aboriginal tribe has not lived continously on the land.
However, the government plans to amend the native title laws and is under pressure from farmers to ensure pastoral leases extinquish native title regardless of aboriginal occupation.
Williams said Placer had lodged a notice of intention to become a party to the native title land claim application, which has been accepted by the National Native Title Tribunal.
He said this would allow Placer to sit in on any hearings to the land claim. "This is not going to affect our planning for the project in any way," he said.
Osborne started production in 1995. The mine produced 35,121 ounce of gold and 31,415 tonnes of copper concentrates in the nine months to September 30, 1996.
The Osborne land claim follows the aboriginal native title land claim lodged last week against the Ernest Henry copper and gold project, also in northwest Queensland.

MIM Holdings Ltd, operator of Ernest Henry, said represenatives to the claim from the Mitakoodi Juhnjlar Aboriginal Corp had proposed that the projects partners pay about A$120 million as compensation.
MIM owns 51 percent of Ernest Henry and Savage Resources Ltd holds the balance.

Queensland has also been the centre for another land claim controversy. RTZ-CRA's plan to develop the A$1 billion Century zinc mine in north Queensland was the subject of a claim in mid-1996 by aboriginal groups.
RTZ-CRA is now negotiating the future of Century under the provisions of the government's native title legislation.
